svg.text: SLAB · how it goes together
Exploded side view (from the right), front of the instrument at the left · 1 mm = 7 px
Build order is bottom-up: keys and strip C into the body, D and battery under them, then the panel
sandwich drops in from the top, the base closes it. Numbers = build steps (12 in total; 8, 9, 10, 12 are
magnets, feet, grille and the hinge strip).
Checked against eng v2 §4.1 (boards A–D), §4.2 (height stack) · budget-variant §v1.4b rev 6 (keys) · common-how-it-works §1, §6
Lid: two laser-stacked leaves (105 + 80), the body's material + leather hinge
frame + 3 mm skin, felt-lined 9 mm cap pocket; end magnets; S-pole sense magnet
Knobs: bought skirted caps (12 mm) + one 26 mm hero; fader caps
push-fit on the pot shafts last of all
Panel sandwich: board A (the panel itself, bare PCB) over board B
pots/switches under A · 11 mm headers · B = the voice · speaker in A/B notch
Body: ≈ 9 laser-cut layers (felt-faced ply), through-bolted
a frame: open over the panel zone and the key zone
Keys: 25 lever tops, owner-cut at Vector Space, on a steel pivot rod
each on a Choc V2 silent switch, magnet in the top; felt top stop
Strip C = the switch board: 25 Choc V2 + 25 standing TO-92 SS49E
its own thin board (keys don't size the main PCB)
Board D (2 Pico 2, DACs, charger, boosts) beside 2 LiPo pouch cells
under the keys, away from the VCOs (eng §4.1)
Base plate, 4 screws: open it to swap the battery (J17)
4 steel discs at the rear catch the stand; 4 felt feet
← player (front)
mm
ASSEMBLED · same scale
34 mm body: control stack 28–32 (eng §4.2) under a panel sunk 4 mm;
keys stack 31–36 with pouch cells. Caps stand 8 mm above the rim.
